passage: Before electric refrigerators were common, many households kept food cold in iceboxes: wooden cabinets lined with tin or zinc and cooled by a large block of ice. In winter, workers cut ice from frozen lakes and stored it in insulated icehouses, and throughout the year it was delivered to homes.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain how people kept food cold before electric refrigerators were common
To argue that iceboxes kept food colder and fresher than modern electric refrigerators
To describe how lakes freeze in winter and why ice from lakes was thick enough to cut
To compare the cost of harvested lake ice with the cost of ice made in factories
steps: The text describes iceboxes and how ice was harvested, stored and delivered.
Its purpose is to explain a past method of keeping food cold.
It never argues that iceboxes were better, never explains how lakes freeze, and never discusses cost.
key: Purpose questions ask why the author wrote the text: to explain, argue, describe or compare.
